title: The Call After the Layoff
script: Dewi: [thoughtful] Aisyah, I got your message. How are you actually doing, beyond the version you texted everyone in the group chat?
Aisyah: Honestly, not great. I keep replaying the meeting, wondering what I could have said differently to change the outcome.
Dewi: [carefully] From everything you've described, this sounds like it was decided well before that meeting even started. There likely wasn't a version of it you could have talked your way out of.
Aisyah: Logically, I know that. Emotionally, I keep constructing scenarios where I'm somehow the exception to a decision that had nothing to do with my performance.
Dewi: [reflective] That's an understandable instinct. Blaming yourself, however unfairly, probably feels more bearable than accepting how arbitrary the whole thing actually was.
Aisyah: That's exactly it. If it's my fault, at least it's within my control. If it's arbitrary, I have no idea what to even fix going forward.
Dewi: [honestly] You don't need to fix anything right this moment. You're allowed to just be upset for a while before jumping straight to strategy.
Aisyah: I feel guilty even taking that time, like I should already be updating my resume and applying somewhere new.
Dewi: [gently] Guilt is not a productivity requirement. Give yourself the week you clearly need before forcing yourself into job-search mode.
Aisyah: Do you really think I'll be okay? Right now it genuinely doesn't feel that way.
Dewi: [calmly] I do, honestly, though I understand that reassurance means very little from the inside of a bad week like this one.
Aisyah: It actually does help, more than you probably realize. I've been sitting alone with this since yesterday, assuming everyone had already moved on with their own lives.
Dewi: [encouraging] Nobody's moved on. I've just been waiting for you to be ready to talk about it, rather than pushing before you wanted to.
Aisyah: Thank you for that patience. Can we talk again tomorrow? I think I'll need this more than once this week.
Dewi: [seriously] Every single day, if that's what you need. I'm not going anywhere.

quiz.question: What does Aisyah keep doing since the meeting?
options: Ignoring what happened completely
Replaying the meeting, wondering what she could have said differently
Planning a celebration
Blaming her manager loudly
quiz.explanation: Aisyah keeps replaying the meeting, wondering what she could have said differently to change the outcome.

quiz.question: What does Dewi suggest about the timing of the layoff decision?
options: It was decided spontaneously during the meeting
It was entirely Aisyah's fault
It had nothing to do with the company
It sounds like it was decided well before the meeting even started
quiz.explanation: Dewi says this sounds like it was decided well before the meeting started, not something Aisyah could have changed.

quiz.question: Why does Dewi say self-blame might feel more bearable than accepting arbitrariness?
options: If it's her fault, at least it's within her control; if arbitrary, there's nothing to fix
Self-blame is always accurate
Self-blame has no emotional function
It doesn't feel more bearable at all
quiz.explanation: Dewi explains that if it's her fault, at least it's within her control, whereas arbitrariness leaves nothing clear to fix.

quiz.question: What does Dewi say about guilt and productivity?
options: Guilt should drive immediate job searching
Guilt is not a productivity requirement
Guilt is necessary for recovery
Guilt should be ignored entirely
quiz.explanation: Dewi firmly states that guilt is not a productivity requirement and tells Aisyah to give herself the week she needs.

quiz.question: What had Aisyah assumed before Dewi called?
options: That Dewi was too busy to care
That she would be fired again soon
That everyone had already moved on with their own lives
That no one knew about the layoff
quiz.explanation: Aisyah says she'd been sitting alone with this since yesterday, assuming everyone had already moved on with their own lives.

quiz.question: Why does self-blame feel tempting after the layoff?
options: It creates a sense of control over an arbitrary decision.
It accurately explains every dismissal.
It makes job searching unnecessary.
It protects the company from criticism.
quiz.explanation: The audio supports it creates a sense of control over an arbitrary decision.

quiz.question: What does the friend refuse to demand immediately?
options: An honest account of the meeting.
Another conversation tomorrow.
Any emotional response.
A rapid shift from grief into job-search strategy.
quiz.explanation: The audio supports a rapid shift from grief into job-search strategy.

quiz.question: How does the friend treat guilt about resting?
options: As proof that Aisyah is weak.
As a reason to hide the layoff.
As not being a requirement for productivity.
As evidence the job was deserved.
quiz.explanation: The audio supports as not being a requirement for productivity.

quiz.question: Why does reassurance matter only partly in the exchange?
options: It guarantees a new job quickly.
It proves the decision was fair.
It replaces practical support.
The friend admits it cannot erase an acute bad week.
quiz.explanation: The audio supports the friend admits it cannot erase an acute bad week.

quiz.question: What does waiting for readiness communicate?
options: Friends should never ask questions.
Support can be patient without disappearing.
Silence is the best response to loss.
Strategy matters more than presence.
quiz.explanation: The audio supports support can be patient without disappearing.
